newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis, Palestinians clash in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Israelis, Palestinians clash in West Bank.

text.p: Stone-throwing Palestinians kept up street battles with Israeli soldiers on Sunday but Palestinian police, under the barrels of Israeli tanks, prevented clashes at several West Bank flashpoints.
It was the 11th day of unrest spurred by Israel's breaking ground for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
"I think the majority of the Palestinian forces, policemen, were working with us against the violence in the area," Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said.
He cited the West Bank town of Nablus where Palestinian police barred some 4,000 Arab protesters from reaching Joseph's Tomb, a Jewish shrine guarded by Israeli soldiers.
Israeli tanks ringed self-ruled Nablus in a show of force which Mordechai said he would lift once the Palestinian Authority "joins us fighting the terrorism and violence".
In Ramallah, north of Jerusalem, Palestinian police used clubs to disperse hundreds of protesters heading towards an Israeli roadblock, witnesses said.
But with pockets of violence still scattered across the West Bank, it was too soon to gauge whether the police action was the start of a crackdown Israel has demanded from the Authority.
"No one can imagine it is possible to advance towards peace while there is unrest, incitement, confrontation or, God forbid, terror," Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said.

Levy's office said the European Union's Middle East peace envoy, Miguel Angel Moratinos, delivered a message to the foreign minister from Yasser Arafat in which the Palestinian president pledged to do his best to curb violence.
The most serious clashes on Sunday erupted near the West Bank town of Jenin where Israeli forces used rubber bullets, teargas and a gravel-firing cannon against protesters.

Hospital officials said one Palestinian, aged 15, was in serious conditon after being shot in the chest with live ammunition, another 35 protesters were hit by rubber bullets and several were injured by gravel shot by the armoured vehicle.
The Israeli army said a soldier was slightly wounded by a stone near Nablus as was an Israeli woman near Ramallah.
Violence also flared in Hebron where seven Palestinians were wounded by rubber bullets.

The killing of a Palestinian by Israeli troops on Saturday raised tensions for Land Day, an annual day of protests by Israeli Arabs against land confiscation by the government. Abdullah Khalil Abdullah was the first fatality since the unrest began more than a week ago.

Israeli police sent reinforcements to areas near Arab towns and villages inside Israel but only isolated incidents of stone-throwing were reported during marches on Sunday in which some protesters held Palestinian flags.
Police said at least 25 Israeli Arabs were arrested.
"Israeli Arabs and their leaders deserve full credit," Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told reporters. "They behaved like mature citizens of Israel."
Some 850,000 Arabs live in the Jewish state and the community annually commemorates the killing by Israeli forces of six Arabs during land demonstrations in 1976.
Skirmishes continued near the tomb of the biblical matriarch Rachel in an Israeli enclave next to self-ruled Bethlehem. Soldiers fired rubber bullets, wounding two Arabs, and teargas.
In Gaza, hundreds of Palestinian youths tried to march on an Israeli checkpoint but were held back by Palestinian police.
Soldiers continued to patrol Israeli cities, on alert for suicide bombers nine days after a Moslem militant killed himself and three Israeli women in an attack on a cafe in Tel Aviv.

An Easter message by Michel Sabbah, Roman Catholic Patriarch in Jerusalem, focused on "the evil around us". He said: "Violence is still in the heart and blindness concerning the rights of others is still in the minds of leaders".

At a meeting of Arab foreign ministers in Cairo, Arafat urged Arab states to press on with plans for a special "uniting for peace" session of the U.N. General Assembly to bypass U.S. vetoes of Security Council resolutions critical of Israel.
Arafat said Israel had declared war on the Palestinian people by surrounding Palestinian areas with tanks in response to Palestinians throwing stones in protest at the settlement building.
